frontier.hypothesis: The residual lives in DECLARATION SCOPE, not in statement spelling: moving the per-block dz/dx pairs to function scope (or conversely tightening center_x/center_z/cross_center/cross_point into narrower scopes) changes reg 96's conflict set where no in-block spelling can
frontier.mechanism: s9 exhausted naming, ordering and operand order INSIDE each block with 1,228 measurements and found nothing below 26, and s8 killed the function-scope declaration-ORDER axis. Scope is the one declaration axis neither session touched: it changes where GCC's pseudo births sit relative to the block boundaries, which is what record_one_conflict (global.c:1392) IORs hard_regs_live into reg 96's hard_reg_conflicts on. s1 already measured that block-scoping the single-set dz/dx was worth part of the 64 -> 40 drop, so this axis is known to be live on this function.

frontier.hypothesis: The four s32* parameters are the wrong object model, and a struct/vector parameter type changes the addressing that feeds the multiplies
frontier.mechanism: Every argument is indexed only at [0] and [2] - a 3-component coordinate read with the y component never touched. A struct type would change the load offsets and the base-register pressure feeding the products, which is the one thing 1,228 spellings of the products themselves could not change. Per splat-symbol-names-are-not-evidence the case must be made from base-register/stride evidence in the target asm, not from splat's names.
frontier.next_probe: Read asm/funcs/func_8002E6B0.s and check whether the target's loads for arg0..arg3 use a common base register with a stride (evidence for a struct model) or independent offsets off four distinct bases (evidence against). If the stride evidence is there, spell the struct form and re-measure; if it is not, bank the negative and the object-model axis is closed.
